planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in gritty, sharply drained soil; a pink-flowered color addition to the SunBurst sun rose series.

directions: SunBurst Pink covers a dense, spreading mat of silvery-green foliage with small, five-petaled pink flowers from April into June. It keeps the low, drought-tolerant habit typical of sun roses, making it a good fit for rock gardens, dry slopes, and wall crevices. Let the soil dry somewhat between waterings, since wet, heavy soil invites rot in this species. Shear lightly after the main flush to tidy the mound and sometimes coax a second round of bloom.

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in gritty, sharply drained soil; a white-flowered color addition to the SunBurst sun rose series.

directions: This white-flowered SunBurst selection opens masses of small, clear-white, five-petaled blooms over gray-green foliage from April through June. The trailing, mounded habit works well cascading over rock walls or spilling from raised beds, and the plant tolerates poor, lean soil better than rich garden beds. Keep it on the dry side between waterings to avoid crown rot, and divide congested clumps every few years to keep the mat vigorous.

common_name: Butterfly Garden Plum Perfect Spanish Lavender

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings/plugs in spring once frost danger passes, in sharply drained soil; part of the new Butterfly Garden Spanish lavender series.

directions: Plum Perfect carries deep plum-purple flower spikes topped with showy upright bracts resembling butterfly wings, blooming from March through July on a compact, well-branched plant. Like other Spanish lavenders it resents soggy soil, so plant in a lean, fast-draining mix and let it dry out between waterings. Monthly feeding during active growth keeps bloom coming, and a light shearing after the first flush often triggers a second round of color. Protect in a container over winter at the cold end of its range.

common_name: Butterfly Garden Poppin' Pink Spanish Lavender

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings/plugs in spring once frost danger passes, in sharply drained soil; a bright-pink sibling in the new Butterfly Garden Spanish lavender series.

directions: Poppin' Pink produces abundant vivid pink flower spikes with upright, butterfly-like bracts on a tidy, mounded plant, flowering from March into July. Pollinators visit the blooms readily, while deer tend to leave the aromatic foliage alone. Grow in full sun with gritty, fast-draining soil, watering sparingly since wet feet quickly cause rot in Spanish lavender. In zones at the cold edge of its range, a sheltered site or winter container protection improves survival.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plugs in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil with some afternoon shade in hot climates; a white-flowered selection from the cold-tolerant Marto mossy-saxifrage series.

directions: Marto White forms a tight, moss-like cushion of small rosettes studded with masses of pure white, long-lasting flowers from March through June. The low mounded habit suits rock gardens, trough plantings, and early spring containers where its cold tolerance lets it color up before most other alpines. Give it gritty, humus-rich soil that drains well but doesn't bake dry, and provide light afternoon shade in warmer parts of its range to prevent the foliage cushion from scorching. Divide congested clumps after flowering to keep the mat fresh.
